crit: Well-known benchmark datasets with a wide range of sample sizes and imbalance ratios; 42 low- and high-dimensional datasets, of which 12 high-dimensional microarray datasets are those reported in Maldonado et al. [6] and 30 low-dimensional ones come from UCI and KEEL; the empirical analysis is meant to confirm FW-SMOTE's behaviour on low- and high-dimensional datasets.
benchmark_inherited_from: Maldonado et al. [6] (S. Maldonado, J. Lopez, C. Vairetti, An alternative SMOTE oversampling strategy for high-dimensional datasets, Appl. Soft Comput. 2019) for the 12 high-dimensional microarray datasets; no source stated for the list of 30 low-dimensional UCI/KEEL datasets
notes: Table 1 (main p.7) prints IR, #Att, #Samples and %class(min.,maj.); no minority count and no class count (all tasks are binary: appendix tables say 'binary classification'). Several Table 1 rows are internally inconsistent: bhat1-bhat4 all IR 9.15 but %min 9.9/8.4/10.3/3.0; car1-car4 all IR 14.8 but %min 6.3/6.9/4.0/3.4; glass-0-6 vs 5 printed (91.7, 8.3) (reversed); solar printed '(4.9.95.1)'; ecoli (10.4, 89.0) and glioma (14.0,86.7) do not sum to 100. Binarised coded from the KEEL two-class file names (e.g. ecoli-0-1 vs 5); bhat1-4 and car1-4 look like several binary versions of one microarray source, but the paper does not describe how they were built (taken from [6]); 'Other' source = the 12 microarray datasets taken from prior work [6] with no repository named. Natural not coded: the paper never says any dataset is natively two-class. method-target in basis is a judgement from the paper's framing (high-dimensional weakness of SMOTE; study on low- and high-dimensional datasets), not an explicit selection sentence. Results: per-dataset values only in the supplementary Appendix A (Tables A.1-A.6; best parameter configuration per method; N chosen as best of N=1/N=3 on average test performance). Table A.4 (k-NN, G-mean) is on supplementary pdf p.4 = printed p.32 (the outcome rows' pdf hints p.1/p.3 are wrong). Code at github.com/cvairetti (code only).
